title: Macramé that sells: cord, knots, cord maths and safe hangers

say: Macramé that sells: cord, knots, cord maths, and safe plant hangers.
This is the video for module one of Advanced Home Décor and Upcycling.
Macramé is making textiles by knotting cords. Every piece, from a key holder to a two-metre wall hanging, is a handful of knots repeated in patterns.

say: Single-strand cotton brushes into a soft, fluffy fringe, but frays as you work. 3-ply twisted cotton suits wall hangings and plant hangers. Tape its ends, or they unravel.

panel.heading: Cord types and thickness
items: Single-strand cotton: fluffy fringes
3-ply cotton: hangings, wavy fringe
Braided cord: hangers that carry weight
Upcycled T-shirt yarn or ankara strips
4 to 5 mm suits most hangings and hangers

say: Braided cord is strong for hangers that carry weight. Upcycled T-shirt yarn or ankara strips make chunky baskets and mats, but the thickness varies.

say: 3 mm cord suits coasters. 4 to 5 mm is the most common for hangings and hangers. Feel the cord first: cotton is soft and takes dye, nylon is slippery.

say: The lark's head mounts each cord on the dowel or ring, folded in half, giving you two working strands.

panel.heading: Six knots cover nearly everything

Half square knot: twists into a spiral
Double half hitch: raised lines
Overhand and gathering knots: ends, bundles

say: The square knot uses four strands. The middle two are fillers that stay still. Tie one half, then the mirror half, and it lies flat.

say: Tie only the first half again and again, and it twists naturally into a spiral. That is the half square knot.

say: For a double half hitch, hold one cord tight as a guide, and wrap each working cord around it twice. A row makes a crisp line.

panel.rule: Even tension, not speed, makes work look professional.

say: Running out of cord midway is the most common beginner frustration. For example, Bisi in Ibadan wants a hanging 60 cm long, with 16 cords. Each working strand needs about 4 times the finished length: 240 cm.

panel.heading: Bisi cuts cord for a wall hanging
items: Finished length x 4: 60 x 4 = 240 cm
Folded, so x 2: 480 cm, or 4.8 m per cord
16 cords x 4.8 m = 76.8 m
Add about 10%: plan for 85 m, one batch

say: The lark's head folds each cord in half, so she cuts 480 cm, or 4.8 m, per cord. That is about 8 times the finished length.

say: Sketch the hanging first, in three zones. The header holds the cords in order. The body carries the pattern, such as diagonal hitch lines meeting in a diamond. The fringe gives shape.

panel.heading: Plan three zones, then finish well
items: Header: holds the cords in order
Body: the pattern and focal point
Fringe: a V, a curve or a straight line
Count knots after every row
Photograph with measurements in the caption

say: A missed knot becomes obvious once the piece hangs, and is hard to undo. After each row, count the knots against your sketch, and look from two metres away.

say: Pass 8 cords through a ring to get 16 strands, bind them with a gathering knot, and split them into 4 arms of 4.

panel.heading: Ada sizes a hanger for a 15 cm pot
items: 8 cords through a ring: 16 strands, 4 arms
Circumference: 3.14 x 15 = about 47 cm
Joining knots, with the pot in hand
Load test: filled pot, one minute

say: For example, Ada in Port Harcourt has a pot 15 cm across. Its circumference is 3.14 times 15, about 47 cm. With 4 joining knots, each gap is about 12 cm.

panel.heading: Ada sizes a hanger for a 15 cm pot
items: 8 cords through a ring: 16 strands, 4 arms
Circumference: 3.14 x 15 = about 47 cm

say: She ties the joining rows, slides the pot in, and only then tightens the bottom gathering knot.

say: Then she lifts the filled pot, with soil, plant and water, by the ring for one minute, and checks for slipping knots.

say: A wet pot of soil is much heavier than it looks. Use strong cord and a solid ring, and tell buyers to hang it from a ceiling hook fixed into a joist, a solid beam, or a wall bracket rated for the load.

panel.heading: Weight and hooks
left: Ceiling hook in a joist or beam
A card with maximum pot size
right: Hang over beds or baby cots

say: Never from a curtain rod or a plastic hook. And never over beds, baby cots or walkways, where someone could be hurt if it falls.

panel.heading: Weight and hooks
left: Ceiling hook in a joist or beam

right: Hang over beds or baby cots

say: To remember. Use 4 to 5 mm cotton for most pieces, and keep tension even. Cut each folded cord about 8 times the finished length. Size hangers to the pot, and test them.
Keep every off-cut over 40 cm for coasters and charms.
